name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information 
system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows 
citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions 
found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the 
streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: 
https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source 
software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS 
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, 
and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. 
The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through 
that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin 
(which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the 
following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is 
also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its 
file path on the server). The possible problem categories are: 
• Waterworks – Drinking water 
• Architectural Barriers 
• Sewerage 
• Public Lighting 
• Waste 
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights 
• Roads and Urban Furniture 
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds 
• Other 
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want 
the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).  

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE 
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the 
Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted 
or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, 
Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which 
point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once 
the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue 
resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be 
set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the 
technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation 
from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).  
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for 
example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), 
two cases are possible: - Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the 
report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the 
report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance 
workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to 
the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer 
can mark the report as resolved. 
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company 
(bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if 
previously configured by the municipal administrator. - Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company 
updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff 
member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state. 


C. CITIZEN UPDATES 
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding 
their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a 
notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators 
updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can 
reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each 
time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be 
disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). 
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the 
Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the 
citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by 
category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was 
chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.  
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into 
Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the 
same rules as for their own reports). 


D. STATISTICS 
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated 
section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, 
or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to 
administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: The Registered Citizen aims to submit detailed reports about urban problems, including location, description, category, and photos, to the public administration.
The Registered Citizen seeks the option to submit reports anonymously to protect their identity while contributing to urban improvement.
The Registered Citizen desires to receive timely notifications and updates on the status changes and progress of their submitted reports.
The Registered Citizen wants to view and follow other citizens' reports to stay informed about broader urban issues and their resolution.
The Non-Registered User aims to view public reports on an interactive map and in a summary table to understand urban inconveniences in Turin.
The Non-Registered User seeks to access public statistics to understand the frequency and trends of reported urban issues.
The Organization Office Staff aims to perform a preliminary review of citizen reports to accept or reject them based on predefined criteria.
The Organization Office Staff needs to provide mandatory written explanations for rejected reports to maintain transparency and trust with citizens.
The Technical Office Staff aims to assign approved reports to responsible parties and manage their lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'.
The Technical Office Staff seeks to exchange information and comments with external maintenance personnel to ensure effective resolution of assigned reports.
The External Maintenance Personnel aims to receive and manage assigned reports within the system, updating their status as work progresses.
The External Maintenance Personnel seeks to exchange information and comments with the Technical Office Staff regarding ongoing interventions.
The Municipal Administrator aims to configure system settings, such as automatic report assignment rules, to optimize operational efficiency.
The Municipal Administrator seeks to access detailed public and private statistics, charts, and tables to monitor system performance and urban issue resolution trends.
lowLevelGoals: The system must allow a Registered Citizen to create a new urban inconvenience report by providing its geographical location, a textual description, and selecting a predefined category.
The system must provide an interface for a Registered Citizen to attach one or more photographic evidences to their urban inconvenience report.
The system must allow a Registered Citizen to explicitly choose whether their identity should be hidden when submitting a report.
The system must send automated notifications to a Registered Citizen whenever the status of one of their submitted reports is updated (e.g., 'Accepted', 'In Progress', 'Resolved').
The system must allow a Registered Citizen to access a chronological log of all status changes and updates related to their submitted reports.
The system must provide a searchable and filterable list of urban inconvenience reports submitted by other Registered Citizens, excluding those marked as private.
The system must allow a Registered Citizen to subscribe to updates for any public report, ensuring they receive notifications about its progress.
The system must display public urban inconvenience reports as markers on an interactive map interface, allowing Non-Registered Users to explore issues geographically.
The system must present public urban inconvenience reports in a tabular format, providing key details at a glance for Non-Registered Users.
The system must provide Non-Registered Users with access to aggregated data and charts showing the distribution and frequency of reported urban issues by category and over time.
The system must provide the Organization Office Staff with a dedicated interface to view all newly submitted reports awaiting preliminary review.
The system must enable the Organization Office Staff to change the status of a pending report to 'Accepted' after review.
The system must enable the Organization Office Staff to change the status of a pending report to 'Rejected' after review.
The system must prompt the Organization Office Staff to provide a textual explanation whenever a report is marked as 'Rejected', making it a mandatory field.
The system must provide the Technical Office Staff with access to all reports that have been marked as 'Accepted' by the Organization Office Staff.
The system must enable the Technical Office Staff to select and assign an approved report to an internal team or an external maintenance company.
The system must allow the Technical Office Staff to change the status of an assigned report to 'In Progress' when work begins.
The system must allow the Technical Office Staff to change the status of a report to 'Resolved' once the issue has been addressed.
The system must provide a mechanism for the Technical Office Staff to post comments and share relevant information directly on a report, visible to assigned external maintenance personnel.
The system must display comments and information posted by external maintenance personnel on assigned reports to the Technical Office Staff.
The system must provide External Maintenance Personnel with access to a dashboard or list showing all urban inconvenience reports specifically assigned to their company.
The system must enable External Maintenance Personnel to change the status of a report assigned to them to 'In Progress' when they begin working on it.
The system must enable External Maintenance Personnel to change the status of a report assigned to them to 'Resolved' once the intervention is complete.
The system must provide a communication channel for External Maintenance Personnel to post comments and provide updates on assigned reports, visible to the Technical Office Staff.
The system must display comments and information posted by the Technical Office Staff on assigned reports to the External Maintenance Personnel.
The system must provide an interface for the Municipal Administrator to define and modify criteria for automatically assigning incoming reports to specific internal teams or external companies.
The system must provide the Municipal Administrator with access to all publicly available statistics, charts, and data tables related to urban issues.
The system must provide the Municipal Administrator with access to internal, sensitive statistics, charts, and data tables related to system performance and operational metrics.

baselineCritiques.actors: The extracted actors are comprehensive and accurately reflect the roles defined in the software description. The distinction between Registered Citizens and Non-Registered Users is appropriate given the different capabilities (submitting reports vs. viewing only). The internal municipal roles (Organization Office, Technical Office, Administrator) and the external role (Maintenance Personnel) are correctly identified based on their specific responsibilities in the report lifecycle and system configuration. No significant omissions or contradictions were found.

high_level_goal.name: Allow citizens to track other urban issues
high_level_goal.description: The Registered Citizen wants to view and follow other citizens' reports to stay informed about broader urban issues and their resolution.

actor.name: Registered Citizen
actor.description: Registers in the system, submits reports with details and photos, chooses anonymity, receives notifications and updates on their reports, views public reports, follows other citizens' reports, and manages personal settings.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Allow citizens to track other urban issues'. 

1. **llg_001** ('Allow Registered Citizen to browse a list of all public reports...') aligns with the requirement in Section C ('CITIZEN UPDATES') that states: 'Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table... Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.' While the HLG focuses on 'tracking', browsing is the prerequisite for identifying issues to track. The description mentions 'excluding those marked as private', which is consistent with the system's logic where only accepted reports become visible on the portal (Section C: 'after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible'). Although the spec doesn't explicitly use the word 'private' for reports, it implies visibility rules based on status and anonymity. This LLG is a valid functional decomposition.

2. **llg_002** ('Enable Registered Citizen to 'follow' specific public reports...') directly addresses the core of the HLG. Section C explicitly states: 'Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).' This LLG captures the subscription/notification mechanism for third-party reports.

There are no contradictions, duplications, or unrelated goals. The missing capability of viewing the *map* view specifically is arguably covered under the general 'browse' or 'view' intent of llg_001, or could be considered a UI detail rather than a distinct functional goal in this context. However, since llg_001 mentions 'list', one might argue the map view is missing. But looking at the HLG 'track other urban issues', the 'follow' mechanism (llg_002) is the critical tracking feature. The browsing (llg_001) enables discovery. The spec says citizens can view maps and tables. llg_001 says 'browse a list'. Is 'list' sufficient for 'map'? The HLG is about tracking. The map is a view. The list is a view. The 'follow' action is the key differentiator for 'tracking'. Given the conservative instruction to keep LLGs unless clearly unsupported/misleading, and that 'browse' is a reasonable abstraction for accessing the public report data (whether via list or map), and llg_002 covers the specific 'tracking' (following) aspect, the set is sufficient. No essential capability is clearly missing that would invalidate the branch. The 'map' view is a presentation detail of the 'browse' capability. Therefore, the goals are kept.

Without an LLG ensuring the system captures this explanation, the HLG's intent (validity based on criteria, which includes justification for rejection) is not fully supported. Therefore, this is a missing essential capability.

Since there is a missing essential capability, the decision is to defer the branch to the normal repair cycle by reporting the missing capability. No LLGs are unsupported or misleading; they are just incomplete.

high_level_goal.name: Efficiently manage report resolution workflow
high_level_goal.description: The Technical Office Staff aims to assign approved reports to responsible parties and manage their lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'.

actor.name: Technical Office Staff
actor.description: Receives approved reports, assigns them to responsible parties, plans interventions, updates report statuses (e.g., 'Work in Progress', 'Resolved'), closes reports, and exchanges information with external maintenance personnel.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately reflect the core responsibilities of the Technical Office Staff as defined in the project description and the parent High-Level Goal (HLG). 

1. **llg_001 (Retrieve approved reports)**: Directly supports the HLG's aim to manage the workflow starting from approved reports. The documentation states that after approval, reports move to 'In Progress' and are assigned. Retrieval is a prerequisite for assignment.
2. **llg_002 (Assign report)**: Explicitly mentioned in the HLG description ('assign approved reports to responsible parties') and the actor description. The documentation confirms assignment to technical offices or external companies.
3. **llg_003 (Update status to 'In Progress')**: The documentation states: 'After approval, accepted reports move to the "In Progress" state... Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to "Work in Progress"'. While the documentation implies a transition from 'In Progress' to 'Work in Progress', the HLG explicitly mentions managing the lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'. The actor description lists updating statuses including 'Work in Progress'. Although 'Work in Progress' is a distinct state in the documentation, 'In Progress' is the initial state after assignment. The LLG is valid as it covers the initial activation of the workflow. Note: The documentation says 'Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to "Work in Progress"'. It does not explicitly say the Technical Office sets it to 'In Progress' manually; it says they move to 'In Progress' *after* approval. However, the HLG explicitly includes 'In Progress' in the scope. Therefore, this LLG is consistent with the HLG.
4. **llg_004 (Update status to 'Resolved')**: The documentation states: 'When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report.' and 'a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.' This is a core capability.

There are no duplicates, contradictions, or unrelated goals. The granularity is appropriate for a low-level goal decomposition. No essential capabilities are missing for the specific scope of the HLG (which focuses on assignment and lifecycle management from In Progress to Resolved). The 'Work in Progress' state is part of the lifecycle, but the HLG description specifically highlights 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'. Even if 'Work in Progress' is a distinct step, the current LLGs cover the start and end of the technical office's active management phase. The absence of a specific LLG for 'Work in Progress' or 'Suspended' does not make the existing ones unsupported or misleading, as they are valid sub-goals. The HLG description says 'manage their lifecycle from "In Progress" to "Resolved"', which encompasses the intermediate states. The current LLGs are sufficient to support the HLG's intent without being misleading.

replacement_request.generation_project_description: In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed to enable citizen participation in urban management. Citizens register with a username, first name, and last name, and confirm via email. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (saved with latitude and longitude) and filling a form with mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (from a predefined list), and one to three photos. After entering the information, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous. If chosen, the citizen's name will not appear in the public list of all reports; instead, 'anonymous' is displayed. Accepted reports become visible on the portal's interactive map and summary table, showing the reporter's name (or 'anonymous') and the report title. Non-registered users can also view these public reports.

replacement_request.generation_project_description: In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed to enable citizen participation in urban environment management. Citizens submit reports on issues like potholes or broken lights. The report lifecycle includes a 'Pending Approval' state where the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review. During this review, reports are marked as either accepted or rejected. The system requires that when a report is rejected, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory. This documentation is crucial for transparency and trust. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. The Organization Office Staff is responsible for this preliminary review and the provision of mandatory written explanations for rejected reports.

Both goals describe the same bidirectional functional intention: the exchange of information and comments between the Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel. According to the calibration rules, one should not keep several HLGs that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants or duplicate the same functional intent from different actor perspectives when the core function is identical. The goal for the Technical Office Staff is essentially the mirror image of the goal for the External Maintenance Personnel. To avoid redundancy and maintain a clean goal model, the duplicate intention should be removed, as the communication aspect is already captured by the External Maintenance Personnel's goal, or it can be argued that the 'Efficiently manage report resolution workflow' goal for the Technical Office Staff covers the management aspect, while the specific communication channel is a shared feature. Given the instruction to remove when another HLG covers the same functional intention, and considering the bidirectional nature of the communication, keeping both is redundant. The 'Streamline communication...' goal is more specific to the interaction. Therefore, the Technical Office Staff's specific goal for this interaction is redundant.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizen Account Management' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies ongoing management beyond just registration. However, the original goal is reasonably scoped to the initial access phase. The description 'To gain access to the system's features and participate in urban management' accurately reflects the purpose of registration. There is no other HLG for the Registered Citizen that covers the specific intention of establishing an account. Therefore, the original goal is kept as it is faithful to the requirements and distinct from other goals. The parent HLG 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' covers the lifecycle of user account interaction: registration, authentication, and profile management. The documentation states that citizens register with a username, first name, and last name, receive a confirmation email, and must confirm via a link to activate the account. It also mentions that users can manage personal settings (like uploading a photo or disabling email notifications) in a settings panel. 

The current LLGs are:
1. `llg_001`: Submit personal details to create a new citizen account. This covers the initial registration step.
2. `llg_002`: Authenticate and log into an existing citizen account. This covers the login step.
3. `llg_003`: Update personal profile information. This covers the modification of account details.

However, the documentation explicitly states: 'Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' This 'Account Confirmation' or 'Email Verification' step is a distinct and essential capability required to transition the account from 'pending' to 'active'. Without this, the user cannot 'gain access to the system's features' as stated in the HLG description. The current LLGs do not explicitly cover the confirmation/verification step. `llg_001` is about submitting details, and `llg_002` is about logging in (which implies the account is already active). The act of confirming the email link is a separate functional requirement. Therefore, an essential capability is missing.

branch_007.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently review citizen reports' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that the Organization Office performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Staff to Review and Process Citizen Reports' aligns with this intention. However, there is another existing High-Level Goal for the same actor: 'Provide clear communication for rejected reports'. While this other goal focuses specifically on the explanation aspect, the primary functional intention of the actor is the review and decision-making process (accept/reject). The original goal 'Efficiently review citizen reports' captures the core functional workflow (viewing, examining, deciding) described in the low-level goals. The term 'Efficiently' is slightly subjective but acceptable in a high-level goal context as it implies the purpose of the workflow. The reconstruction is slightly more generic ('Process') but the original is faithful to the 'review' terminology used in the requirements ('preliminary review'). The existing HLG 'Provide clear communication...' is a specific sub-task or constraint of the review process, not a duplicate of the entire review workflow. Therefore, the original HLG is a valid, distinct, and supported intention for the actor. It is not too generic, narrow, or incorrectly scoped. It is not a mere wording variant of the other HLG, as one is about the decision process and the other is about the specific output (explanation) for a subset of decisions (rejections). Thus, it should be kept. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential workflow for the Organization Office Staff to review citizen reports. Specifically: 'Retrieve pending citizen reports' (llg_001) allows staff to identify reports awaiting review; 'Access detailed citizen report information' (llg_002) enables the evaluation of report content; 'Mark a citizen report as accepted' (llg_003) and 'Mark a citizen report as rejected with explanation' (llg_004) cover the decision-making process, including the mandatory written explanation for rejections as required by the documentation. The sibling HLG 'Provide clear communication for rejected reports' focuses on the transparency aspect for citizens, but the capability to *provide* the explanation is inherently part of the rejection action described in the parent HLG and correctly captured in llg_004. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are contradicted by the documentation.

replacement_request.generation_project_description: In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed. branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which explicitly details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Provide User Account Management for Citizens' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies administrative functions not strictly belonging to the citizen's primary intent of participation. The original goal is correctly scoped to the specific functional intention of gaining access via registration. It is distinct from 'Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences' (the action taken after registration) and other goals. Therefore, the original goal is faithful and appropriately scoped. The parent HLG 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' covers the lifecycle of user account creation and access. The documentation states: 'Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' 

The current LLGs are:
1. llg_001: Submit personal details to create a new citizen account. (Covers registration input).
2. llg_002: Authenticate and log into an existing citizen account. (Covers login/access).
3. llg_003: Update personal profile information. (Covers maintenance of account details, supported by 'user settings panel' mention in Section C, though primarily associated with settings, updating profile info is a standard part of account management and not explicitly excluded. However, looking closely at the documentation, Section C mentions 'user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo'. This is a specific capability. Is it essential to 'register and create'? Usually, 'create' implies the initial setup. 'Update' is maintenance. The HLG name is 'register and create'. The description is 'To gain access...'. 

Let's re-evaluate the missing capability. The documentation explicitly states: 'The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' This is a critical step in the *creation* process. Without confirmation, the account is not valid. LLG_001 says 'Submit personal details to create...'. It does not explicitly mention the confirmation step. Is 'Confirming registration via email link' a distinct low-level goal? Yes, it is a distinct action required to complete the creation process. The current LLGs jump from 'Submit details' to 'Authenticate'. The confirmation step is missing. 

However, often 'Create Account' LLGs encompass the entire flow including confirmation. But in Goal-Oriented RE, if the confirmation is a distinct user action (clicking a link), it might be a separate goal or part of the creation goal. Let's look at the wording of llg_001: 'Enable a citizen to provide their name, email, and password to register and create a new user account in the system.' This describes the input phase. The confirmation phase is 'Confirming the registration'. 

Is there another missing capability? The documentation mentions 'username, first name, and last name'. LLG_001 mentions 'name, email, and password'. It misses 'username' and 'last name' specifically, but 'name' is vague. More importantly, the *confirmation* step is a mandatory gate. 

Let's check if 'Confirming registration' is considered part of 'Creating'. If I submit details, I haven't created a *valid* account yet. I have created a *pending* account. The goal is to 'create a personal account' (implied valid). The confirmation is essential. 

Let's look at the sibling HLGs. None cover registration. 

Is 'Confirming registration via email link' a material defect if missing? Yes, because the system explicitly states the user can only use the system *after* confirming. LLG_001 only covers the submission. LLG_002 covers login. There is no LLG for the confirmation step. 

Therefore, the capability 'Confirm registration via email link' is missing. 

Wait, let's look at the evaluation examples. 'Atomic API-mappable LLGs'. 'Confirm registration' is an atomic action. 'Submit registration' is an atomic action. They are distinct. 

So, `missing_essential_capabilities` should include 'Confirm registration via email link'. 

Also, LLG_001 mentions 'password'. The documentation says 'registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name'. It does *not* explicitly mention a password in the registration section (Section A). It says 'username, first name, and last name'. Then 'email with a confirmation link'. It doesn't explicitly say 'password' is collected during registration, although it's implied for login (LLG_002 mentions password). However, standard practice and the login LLG imply it. But strictly based on the text: 'registered... with a username, first name, and last name'. It does not list password. However, LLG_002 requires a password to log in. So the password must be set somewhere. Usually during registration. So LLG_001 including password is reasonable. 

The main gap is the confirmation step. 

Decision: REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS.

branch_008.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Provide clear communication for rejected reports' is supported by the project description, which mandates a written explanation for rejected reports to ensure transparency. However, the phrasing 'Provide clear communication' is slightly broader and less precise than the specific functional requirement of documenting the rationale. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Ensure reasons for report rejection are documented' is more faithful to the specific constraint (mandatory written explanation) and aligns better with the actor's duty to record the rationale. While the original is not incorrect, the reconstruction offers a tighter, more accurate scope that avoids ambiguity about the nature of the 'communication' (it is a record of rationale, not just a message). Therefore, a rewrite to align with the precise documentation requirement is preferred for clarity and fidelity to the 'mandatory written explanation' constraint.

The project description explicitly states that 'a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory' when a report is rejected. Therefore, the goal must be refined to explicitly capture the requirement to document this mandatory written rationale/explanation, ensuring the HLG aligns with the specific functional constraint rather than a general quality attribute.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed to enable citizen participation in urban environment management. Citizens submit reports on issues like potholes or broken lights. The report lifecycle includes a 'Pending Approval' state where the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review. During this review, reports are marked as either accepted or rejected. The system requires that when a report is rejected, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory. This explanation serves as the documented rationale for the rejection decision.

actor.description: Performs preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected, and provides mandatory written explanations for rejected reports.

branch_009.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage report resolution workflow' is supported by the project description, which details the Technical Office Staff's role in assigning reports, planning interventions, updating statuses (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved), and closing reports. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Technical Office Staff to Manage and Track the Resolution of Accepted Reports' captures the same functional intention. The original goal is reasonably scoped and not overly generic. While the word 'Efficiently' is slightly subjective, it aligns with the operational nature of the task. There is no other HLG for this actor that covers the core lifecycle management (assignment, status updates, closure) distinct from the specific collaboration goal ('Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance'). Therefore, the original goal is valid and should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) cover the core workflow of retrieving approved reports, assigning them, and updating their status to 'In Progress' and 'Resolved'. However, the parent HLG description explicitly states the goal is to 'manage their lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved''. The documentation (Section B) defines the possible states as: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. The actor description for Technical Office Staff explicitly mentions updating statuses such as 'Work in Progress'. The current LLGs omit the capability to update the status to 'Work in Progress' (which indicates the issue resolution has started after planning) and 'Suspended' (for organizational/technical reasons). While 'Suspended' might be considered an edge case, 'Work in Progress' is a distinct, documented state in the lifecycle that the actor is explicitly responsible for updating, and it is missing from the current decomposition. Therefore, the decomposition is incomplete regarding the explicit lifecycle management capabilities defined in the parent HLG and documentation.

branch_010.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. However, there is a significant semantic overlap with the existing High-Level Goal 'Streamline communication during external interventions' assigned to the 'External Maintenance Personnel' actor. Both goals describe the same bidirectional functional intention: the exchange of information and comments between the Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, a single functional interaction (communication channel) should not be split into two separate high-level goals for the two actors involved if the core intention is the same (collaborative communication on reports). The existing goal for External Maintenance Personnel ('Streamline communication...') already captures this interaction. Keeping both would result in redundant HLGs that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants from different perspectives. Therefore, the original HLG for Technical Office Staff should be removed to avoid duplication, as the functional requirement is already covered by the counterpart's goal or can be subsumed under the general workflow management if strictly necessary, but given the specific 'Streamline communication' HLG exists, removal is the cleanest action to prevent redundancy.

However, the term 'external parties' is slightly ambiguous compared to the specific actor 'External Maintenance Personnel', and 'manage assigned tasks' is a bit generic. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable External Maintenance Personnel to Manage Assigned Urban Inconvenience Reports' is more precise and faithful to the domain context (urban inconvenience reports). While the original is not incorrect, the reconstruction offers better specificity and alignment with the actor's specific role in the system. However, looking at the other HLGs, there is already 'Streamline communication during external interventions' for the same actor. The original HLG covers the status management aspect (receiving, updating status), which is distinct from the communication aspect. Therefore, the intention is valid and distinct. The original name is acceptable but could be slightly more specific. branch_012.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Streamline communication during external interventions' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. However, there is a significant semantic overlap with the existing High-Level Goal for the Technical Office Staff: 'Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance', which describes the same bidirectional communication channel from the other actor's perspective. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, a single functional requirement (the communication channel) should not be split into two separate high-level goals for two actors if they represent the same system capability. The existing HLG for Technical Office Staff ('Facilitate collaboration...') is already present. Keeping both would result in redundant goals that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants. Therefore, the original HLG for External Maintenance Personnel should be removed to avoid redundancy, as the functional intention is already covered by the counterpart's goal or can be subsumed under the general workflow management goals. Alternatively, if we consider the actor-specific perspective strictly, the 'Enable external parties to manage assigned tasks' HLG covers the status updates, but the communication aspect is the specific focus here. Given the instruction to 'not keep several HLGs that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants' and the presence of the mirror-image goal for Technical Office Staff, removing the duplicate is the most consistent action to maintain a clean goal model.

replacement_request.rationale: The original HLG 'Provide system configuration capabilities' is too broad and abstract. The specific documented functional intention in Section B (Case 1 Note) is that the Municipal Administrator can configure the automatic assignment of reports in a specific category to an external company, bypassing the initial review. This is a distinct, atomic capability. The reconstructed HLG 'Configure Automatic Report Routing' accurately captures this specific intent. The actor remains the Municipal Administrator. The request focuses on this specific configuration capability without including pipeline internals or a final HLG name.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed. A key operational feature involves handling reports that require intervention by external maintenance companies (e.g., Enel X for Public Lighting). According to the system requirements, if an external company has access to Participium, the technical office can assign reports to them. However, a specific configuration capability exists: the automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to an external company, bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality, is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator. The Municipal Administrator needs to be able to define these routing rules to ensure that specific categories of reports are automatically directed to the appropriate external entities without manual intervention at the approval stage.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizen Account Management' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies ongoing management beyond just registration. However, the original goal is reasonably scoped to the initial access phase. The description 'To gain access to the system's features and participate in urban management' accurately reflects the purpose of registration. There is no other HLG for the Registered Citizen that covers the specific intention of establishing an account. Therefore, the original goal is kept as it is faithful to the requirements and distinct from other goals. The parent HLG 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' covers the lifecycle of user account interaction: registration, authentication, and profile management. The documentation states that citizens register with a username, first name, and last name, receive a confirmation email, and must confirm via a link before the account is valid. It also mentions that users can manage personal settings (like uploading a photo or disabling email notifications) in a settings panel. 

The current LLGs are:
1. `llg_001`: Submit personal details to create a new citizen account. This covers the initial registration step.
2. `llg_002`: Authenticate and log into an existing citizen account. This covers the login step.
3. `llg_003`: Update personal profile information. This covers the modification of account details.

However, the documentation explicitly states: 'Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' This 'Account Confirmation' or 'Email Verification' step is a distinct and essential capability required to transition the account from 'pending' to 'active'. Without this, the user cannot 'gain access to the system's features' as stated in the HLG description. The current LLGs do not explicitly cover the action of confirming the account via the email link. While `llg_001` covers submitting details, it does not cover the subsequent confirmation action which is a prerequisite for the account to be usable. Therefore, the capability to 'Confirm account registration via email link' is missing.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which explicitly details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Provide User Account Management for Citizens' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies administrative functions not strictly belonging to the citizen's primary intent of participation. The original goal is correctly scoped to the specific functional intention of gaining access via registration. It does not overlap with other HLGs for the Registered Citizen, which focus on reporting, tracking, and viewing. Therefore, the original goal is faithful and appropriately scoped. The parent HLG 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' covers the lifecycle of user account creation and access. The documentation states: 'Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' 

The current LLGs are:
1. llg_001: Submit personal details to create a new citizen account. (Covers registration input).
2. llg_002: Authenticate and log into an existing citizen account. (Covers login/access).
3. llg_003: Update personal profile information. (Covers maintenance of account details, including the personal photo mentioned in Section C: 'user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo').

However, there is a critical missing step in the registration lifecycle explicitly described in the documentation: **Email Confirmation**. The text says 'The registration becomes valid... only after confirming through that link.' Without a goal to confirm the account via email, the account is not fully 'created' or 'valid' for use. llg_001 only covers submitting details. It does not cover the confirmation step which is a mandatory part of the registration process before the user can 'use the system'. This is an essential capability required by the parent HLG (creating a *valid* personal account) that is absent from the current LLGs. Therefore, the decomposition is incomplete.

branch_012.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Streamline communication during external interventions' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. However, there is a significant semantic overlap with the existing High-Level Goal for the Technical Office Staff: 'Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance', which describes the same bidirectional communication channel from the other actor's perspective. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, a single functional requirement (the communication channel) should not be split into two separate high-level goals for two actors if they represent the same system capability. The existing HLG for Technical Office Staff ('Facilitate collaboration...') is already present. Keeping both would result in redundant goals that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants. Therefore, the original HLG for External Maintenance Personnel should be removed to avoid redundancy, as the functional intention is already covered by the Technical Office Staff's goal, or the system requirement is singular. Alternatively, one could argue for keeping it if the focus is strictly on the actor's specific need, but the instruction 'Do not keep several HLGs that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants' strongly suggests removing the duplicate. The Technical Office Staff's goal 'Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance' is more comprehensive in naming the collaboration aspect. Thus, removing the External Maintenance Personnel's specific communication goal is the best choice to maintain a non-redundant goal model.

branch_013.rationale: The original High-Level Goal is supported by the project description, specifically the note in Section B stating that automatic assignment to external companies is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator. The actor description also explicitly mentions configuring system settings such as automatic report assignment. The original goal's description ('define and manage rules... thereby streamlining... and bypassing initial manual review') accurately reflects the functional intent and the specific mechanism (bypassing review) described in the text. The bottom-up reconstruction is semantically equivalent but slightly less descriptive regarding the 'bypassing' aspect which is a key feature of this configuration. Therefore, the original goal is faithful, correctly scoped, and distinct from the other HLG for this actor (which focuses on statistics). The parent HLG 'Enable efficient configuration of automatic report assignments' requires the Municipal Administrator to define and manage rules. The current LLGs cover the creation (llg_001), modification (llg_002), and retrieval/viewing (llg_003) of these rules. While 'deletion' is a standard CRUD operation, the documentation does not explicitly mandate the ability to delete rules, only to configure (create/update) them. The core capability of 'managing' rules is sufficiently covered by create, update, and read operations in this context. There are no contradictions with the documentation, and no essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG are missing. The decomposition is complete and accurate.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description's functional requirements are fully covered by the existing High-Level Goals. Citizen registration and reporting are covered by 'Enable citizens to register...' and 'Enable citizens to report...'. The report lifecycle management (review, assignment, status updates) is covered by goals for Organization Office Staff ('Efficiently review...'), Technical Office Staff ('Efficiently manage report resolution workflow...'), and External Maintenance Personnel ('Enable external parties...'). Communication and notification features (notifications, messages, chatbot access) are covered by 'Keep citizens informed about report progress' and 'Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance'. Public visibility and statistics are covered by 'Provide public visibility of urban issues', 'Offer public insights into urban problem trends', and 'Offer comprehensive system performance insights'. The configuration of automatic assignments is covered by 'Enable efficient configuration of automatic report assignments'. No distinct, undocumented functional intention remains uncovered.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which explicitly details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Provide User Account Management for Citizens' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies administrative functions not strictly belonging to the citizen's primary intent of participation. The original goal is correctly scoped to the specific functional intention of gaining access via registration. It does not overlap with other HLGs for the Registered Citizen, which focus on reporting, tracking, and viewing. Therefore, the original goal is faithful and appropriately scoped. The parent HLG 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' covers the lifecycle of user account creation and access. The documentation specifies that registration requires a username, first name, last name, and email (implied by the confirmation link mechanism), and that the account becomes valid only after email confirmation. The current LLGs cover: 1) Submitting details to create an account (llg_001), 2) Authenticating/logging in (llg_002), and 3) Updating profile information (llg_003). 

However, there is a material gap: The documentation explicitly states, 'The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' This implies a distinct capability of 'Confirming account registration via email link' which is a prerequisite for the account to be active and for the user to log in (llg_002). While llg_001 covers the submission of data, it does not explicitly cover the confirmation step which is a mandatory part of the 'create a personal account' process as defined by the system's rules. Without this confirmation step, the account is not fully created/activated. Therefore, the capability to confirm the registration is missing from the current decomposition. Additionally, llg_001 mentions 'password' which is not explicitly listed in the registration fields in Section A (username, first name, last name), but is standard for authentication. However, the missing confirmation step is a more significant functional gap explicitly grounded in the text ('user can use the system only after confirming').

branch_009.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage report resolution workflow' is supported by the project description, which details the Technical Office Staff's role in assigning reports, planning interventions, updating statuses (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved), and closing reports. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Technical Office Staff to Manage and Track the Resolution of Accepted Reports' captures the same functional intention. The original goal is reasonably scoped and not overly generic. While the word 'Efficiently' is slightly subjective, it aligns with the system's purpose of streamlining urban management. There is no other HLG for this actor that covers the core lifecycle management (assignment, status updates, closure) as comprehensively as this one; the other HLG for this actor ('Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance') focuses specifically on communication, which is a subset or parallel aspect, not the main workflow management. Therefore, the original goal is valid and should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) cover the retrieval of approved reports, assignment to responsible parties, and status updates to 'In Progress' and 'Resolved'. However, the parent HLG description explicitly states the goal is to 'manage their lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved''. The documentation (Section B) defines the state 'Work in Progress' as indicating that 'issue resolution has started' after the intervention is planned. The actor description for Technical Office Staff explicitly lists 'updates report statuses (e.g., 'Work in Progress', 'Resolved')'. The current LLGs omit the capability to update the status to 'Work in Progress', which is a distinct state in the lifecycle described in the documentation and explicitly mentioned in the actor's responsibilities. While 'In Progress' is mentioned in the HLG description as the starting point, the transition to 'Work in Progress' is a key part of the management workflow described in the text ('Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to 'Work in Progress''). Therefore, the absence of an LLG for updating to 'Work in Progress' represents a missing essential capability required by the parent HLG and documentation.

replacement_request.rationale: The original HLG used generic terms ('external parties', 'assigned tasks') that did not align with the specific domain language of the Participium system. The reconstruction focuses on the specific actor 'External Maintenance Personnel' and the specific object 'assigned urban inconvenience reports' to accurately reflect the documented functional intention in Section B (Case 1) where these personnel update statuses and exchange comments.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: In the Municipality of Turin, the Participium system allows citizens to report urban inconveniences. When a report is assigned to an external company that has access to the system, the technical office assigns the report to users from that company. External Maintenance Personnel can then move the report from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress', exchange information and comments with technical office staff (visible only to them, not citizens), and mark the report as 'Resolved' once the work is completed.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizen Account Management' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies ongoing management beyond just registration. However, the original goal is reasonably scoped to the initial access phase. The description 'To gain access to the system's features and participate in urban management' accurately reflects the purpose of registration in this context. It does not overlap significantly with other HLGs for the Registered Citizen, which focus on reporting, tracking, and viewing. Therefore, the original goal is kept as it is a distinct and necessary functional intention. The parent HLG 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' covers the lifecycle of user account interaction: registration, authentication, and profile management. The documentation states that citizens register with a username, first name, and last name, receive a confirmation email, and must confirm via a link before the account is valid. It also mentions that users can manage personal settings (like uploading a photo or disabling email notifications) in a settings panel. 

The current LLGs are:
1. `llg_001`: Submit personal details to create a new citizen account. This covers the initial registration step.
2. `llg_002`: Authenticate and log into an existing citizen account. This covers the login step.
3. `llg_003`: Update personal profile information. This covers the modification of account details.

However, the documentation explicitly states: 'Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link.' This 'Account Confirmation' or 'Email Verification' step is a distinct and essential capability required to transition the account from 'pending' to 'active'. Without this, the user cannot 'gain access to the system's features' as stated in the HLG description. The current LLGs do not explicitly cover the action of confirming the account via the email link. While `llg_001` covers submitting details, it does not cover the subsequent confirmation action which is a prerequisite for the account to be usable. Therefore, the capability to 'Confirm account registration via email link' is missing.

high_level_evaluation.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage report resolution workflow' is supported by the project description, which details the Technical Office Staff's role in assigning reports, planning interventions, and updating statuses from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'. However, the description 'assign approved reports to responsible parties and manage their lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'' is slightly narrow as it omits the 'Work in Progress' state explicitly mentioned in the actor description and project text, and the term 'Efficiently' is a subjective quality attribute rather than a functional intention. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Technical Office Staff to Manage and Track Report Resolution' is more faithful to the functional scope (managing the full lifecycle including tracking) and aligns better with standard goal-oriented requirements engineering phrasing. While the original is not incorrect, the reconstruction is more precise and comprehensive regarding the 'tracking' aspect implied by the status updates and collaboration. Therefore, a rewrite is preferred to improve precision and scope coverage.
high_level_evaluation.rewriting_focus: Refine the goal to explicitly cover the management and tracking of the report lifecycle (including assignment, status updates like 'Work in Progress', and resolution) without subjective qualifiers like 'efficiently'.

branch_011.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage assigned urban inconvenience reports' is supported by the project description, which details the workflow for external maintenance personnel (Case 1) to receive assigned reports, update their status (from Assigned to In Progress, and finally to Resolved), and exchange comments with technical office staff. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable External Maintenance Personnel to Manage Assigned Urban Inconvenience Reports' aligns semantically with the original goal, covering the full lifecycle of handling assigned reports. There is no other High-Level Goal for this actor that covers this specific functional intention. The scope is appropriate and faithful to the requirements. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential functionalities required by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) for External Maintenance Personnel. 
1. 'Retrieve assigned urban inconvenience reports' (llg_001) covers the ability to receive/view the list of assigned tasks.
2. 'View details of an assigned report' (llg_002) covers the ability to view specific report information.
3. 'Update status of an assigned report' (llg_003) covers the lifecycle management actions explicitly mentioned in the documentation (moving from Assigned to In Progress, and marking as Resolved).
4. 'Add comments to an assigned report' (llg_004) covers the communication aspect with technical office staff.

The documentation states that external maintenance personnel can 'move the report from Assigned to In Progress' and 'mark the report as resolved'. It also states they 'can exchange information and comments through the report'. The current LLGs capture these actions. While 'viewing comments' is not explicitly a separate LLG, it is typically part of the 'View details' or 'Add comments' interaction flow in such systems, and the primary capability of *exchanging* (sending) is covered. There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG that are absent from the current set. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to register and create a personal account' is supported by the project description, which details the registration process (username, name, email confirmation) as a prerequisite for using the system. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizen Account Management' is broader and potentially overlaps with other goals like 'Keep citizens informed' (which mentions user settings) or implies ongoing management beyond the initial creation. However, the original goal is reasonably scoped to the specific functional intention of gaining access via registration. It is distinct from reporting, tracking, or viewing public data. The description 'To gain access to the system's features and participate in urban management' accurately reflects the purpose of registration in this context. Therefore, the original goal is kept as it is faithful and correctly scoped. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential lifecycle of a citizen account as defined by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) and the project documentation. 
1. **Registration**: LLG_001 covers the submission of personal details (username, first name, last name, email) to initiate account creation, aligning with Section A of the documentation.
2. **Activation**: LLG_002 covers the confirmation via email link, which is explicitly required in Section A ('The registration becomes valid... only after confirming through that link').
3. **Access**: LLG_003 covers authentication/login, which is necessary to 'gain access to the system's features' as stated in the HLG description.
4. **Maintenance**: LLG_004 covers updating personal profile information. Section C mentions that users can 'upload a personal photo' in the user settings panel, which falls under maintaining personal account details. 

There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG. The sibling HLGs cover reporting, notifications, tracking other reports, and public viewing, which are correctly excluded from this branch. The decomposition is atomic, API-mappable, and consistent with the documentation. No contradictions or unsupported claims were found.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description's functional requirements are fully covered by the existing High-Level Goals. Citizen registration and reporting are covered by 'Enable citizens to register...' and 'Enable citizens to report...'. The report lifecycle management (review, assignment, status updates) is covered by goals for Organization Office Staff ('Efficiently review citizen reports', 'Provide clear communication...') and Technical Office Staff ('Efficiently manage report resolution workflow'). Collaboration with external parties is covered by 'Facilitate collaboration with external maintenance' and 'Efficiently manage assigned urban inconvenience reports'. Citizen updates and tracking are covered by 'Keep citizens informed...' and 'Allow citizens to track other urban issues'. Public visibility and statistics are covered by 'Provide public visibility...' and 'Offer public insights...'. Administrative configuration and private statistics are covered by 'Enable efficient configuration...' and 'Offer comprehensive system performance insights'. No distinct, undocumented functional intention remains.
